title: Quarterly planning for the support team (long)
lines: Good afternoon, Omar and Lina. This is our quarterly planning for the Pearl Pay support team. We have three topics today: the chat support hours, the help centre articles, and training for the new refund process. It will be a long one, so let us keep moving.
Sounds good. I brought the numbers from the last quarter, so I can start with chat if you like.

Chat volume went up by about twenty percent compared with the quarter before. Most of the growth is in the evening. Between six and ten in the evening we now get almost a third of all chats, but the team stops answering at eight.
That matches what I see in the complaints. A lot of the angry messages start with something like: I waited all night and nobody answered.
Exactly. After eight, customers leave a message, and we answer the next morning. The average wait for those messages is about thirteen hours.
Thirteen hours is far too long for a payments app. People write to us because a transfer failed or a card was blocked. They need an answer the same evening.
Before we go further, one question the team keeps asking me. Do we need weekend cover as well? Saturdays are quiet, but Fridays can be busy.
Let us hold that thought. It depends on the training plan and on how many people we have, so we will come back to it in the third topic.

Fine. For weekdays, I looked at three options. Option one, keep the hours as they are and add an automatic reply in the evening. Option two, extend the hours to ten in the evening. Option three, answer around the clock.
Around the clock sounds expensive, and the night volume is tiny. I do not think option three makes sense for us yet.
I agree. And the automatic reply alone does not solve anything; it only tells people that they have to wait.
So option two. What would it cost us?
If two agents move their shift two hours later, we cover the evening without hiring anyone. The mornings are quieter than they used to be, so we can afford it.
The agents I spoke to were open to it, as long as the rota is fair and nobody is stuck on evenings every week.
One more number on that. On the days when we tested a late shift in January, the evening wait dropped from thirteen hours to under ten minutes.
And the complaints on those days were about half of a normal day.
Good. Then let us decide it. From the first of March, chat support runs until ten in the evening on weekdays.
Omar, please update the shift rota for March by Thursday, so the agents know their new hours in good time.
Yes, I will send the new rota by Thursday.
Will the rota rotate the evening shifts, so that everyone does them in turn?
That is the plan. Each agent will have about one evening week in four.
Great. Second topic, the help centre. Lina, you looked at the search data.

I did. The most common searches in the help centre are about card payments: declined payments, payments that show twice, and refunds from online shops. For all three we have either no article at all, or an article from two years ago that shows the old app.
That explains a lot of chats. People search, find nothing, and then open a chat.
Yes. When an article exists and is up to date, about half of the people who read it do not contact us afterwards.
That is a strong argument for writing more of them. How many articles are we talking about?
I would start with five new articles about card payments: declined payments, double payments, refunds, payment limits, and paying abroad.
Five sounds right. More than that and we will not finish them this quarter.
Then we publish five new articles about card payments this quarter. That is decided.
Good. I can write the first two articles myself by the end of the month.
Thanks, Lina. The first two by the end of the month.
I will review the old payment articles and mark the ones we should delete.
Thank you. Old articles that show the wrong screens do more harm than good.
One thing I am not sure about. Should the new articles also be in Arabic? Many of our customers would prefer it, but translation takes time, and someone has to check it.
That is a fair question, and I cannot answer it today. It depends on the budget for translation, and I have not seen the budget yet.
Maybe we could translate only the two most read articles first.
Maybe. Let us see what the budget says first.
Right, that stays open for now.
The design team also sent new screenshots of the app last week, so the articles can show the new screens.
Third topic, training for the new refund process. The process changes on the twentieth of March, and every agent has to know it before then.
The main change is that agents can approve refunds up to fifty dinars themselves. Above that, it still goes to the finance team.
That will save a lot of time. Right now even a refund of five dinars waits two days for finance.
Exactly. So we need one training session for everyone, ideally in person, with real cases from the last month.
I can collect ten real cases from last month for the session.
Thank you, Omar. Ten cases are enough.
Sara, can you book the big training room for the fourteenth of March? It is the only room with enough seats.
Yes, I will book the training room for the fourteenth of March today.
Who will actually run the training? It should be someone who knows the refund rules really well.
I honestly do not know yet. Finance might send someone, or we do it ourselves. Let us leave that open until finance replies.
Okay. And now back to my question from the beginning, the weekend cover.
Right. With the evening shifts and the training in March, we do not have enough people for weekends as well. So no weekend cover this quarter. We look at it again in the summer.
Agreed. The team will be glad to have a clear answer.
Thank you. Anything else before we close?
Only that the numbers I showed are in the shared folder, if anyone wants them.
Then thanks, both of you. Good meeting.
